## About Me

I am a Research Fellow at UCL Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health, working in Population Health Improvement UK and the NIHR Children and Families Policy Research Unit. I use national linked administrative data, mainly [ECHILD](https://www.echild.ac.uk/), to evaluate services for children and to study inequalities in young people's access to mental health care.

I completed my PhD at the UCL Social Research Institute in 2026. It evaluated Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hubs and other multi-agency front door services in children's social care across England. I was research lead on the [Evaluation of Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hubs](https://foundations.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/evaluation-of-multi-agency-safeguarding-hubs.pdf), commissioned by the Department for Education. It contributed evidence to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 and was cited in the Sara Sharif Child Safeguarding Practice Review.

I have taught quantitative methods at UCL since 2022 and teach on the Introduction to ECHILD course for researchers using linked data. Before moving into child health and social care, I worked on the measurement of job quality in Latin America and the EU.

## Research Interests

- Evaluating children's services and child protection, including multi-agency safeguarding hubs
- Inequalities in referral and access to NHS mental health services for children and young people
- Intersectional inequalities, using multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy (MAIHDA)
- Linked administrative data across health, education and social care (ECHILD)
- Quasi-experimental methods: difference-in-differences, synthetic controls, interrupted time series
- Reproducible research in R and Quarto
